definitions.explanation: An informal word for one's own wife, typically used by middle-aged and older men. It carries a casual, familiar tone and is used when referring to one's wife to others in relaxed conversation.

examples.japanese: {女房|にょうぼう}に{叱|しか}られた。
examples.english: I got scolded by my wife.

examples.japanese: うちの{女房|にょうぼう}は{料理|りょうり}が{上手|じょうず}だ。
examples.english: My wife is a good cook.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}{連|つ}れ{添|そ}った{女房|にょうぼう}に{先立|さきだ}たれて、{彼|かれ}はすっかり{元気|げんき}をなくした。
examples.english: Having been predeceased by the wife who had been with him for so many years, he completely lost his spirits.

notes:
USAGE:
{女房|にょうぼう} is used by men to refer to their own wife in casual speech. It has a slightly old-fashioned and down-to-earth feel. Younger men tend to prefer {妻|つま} or {嫁|よめ}. It is not used to refer to someone else's wife (use {奥|おく}さん instead).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- うちの{女房|にょうぼう}: my wife (casual)
- {女房|にょうぼう}{役|やく}: a supportive partner/right-hand person
- {恐妻家|きょうさいか}: henpecked husband (related concept)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{妻|つま} is the neutral, standard term. {嫁|よめ} is colloquial and common among younger speakers. {家内|かない} is polite but somewhat dated. {女房|にょうぼう} has the most casual, unpretentious tone among these.

HISTORICAL NOTE:
Originally referred to ladies-in-waiting at the imperial court ({女房|にょうぼう} literally means "woman's room/quarters"). The meaning shifted to "wife" during the Edo period.
